parts.title: Report Repair
parts.summary: Find the two entries in an expense report that sum to 2020 and multiply them together.
parts.algorithmSummary: Generalized sorted k-sum two-pointer search (k = 2 for Part 1, pre-built k = 3+ for zero-churn Part 2) in 2020/day01/shared/ (0.44 ms across 200 entries -> 355,875): immutable ExpenseReport with stable index preservation, exact BigInt product getter, bounded probe trace (kSumTrace.ts), interactive sorted-bar & sum-delta gauge visualizer, differentially verified against an independent brute-force oracle for k = 2 and k = 3.
parts.complexity: O(N log N) time, O(N) space
learnings: Generalizing sorted two-pointer search into recursive k-sum (kSum.ts) with an explicit ProbeObserver keeps Part 1 and Part 2 sharing one 100%-covered engine with zero Part 2 shared edits.
Checking !match rather than !product prevents false negatives when a valid tuple contains 0 (e.g., 0 + 2020 = 2020 has product 0n).

parts.title: Report Repair
parts.summary: Find the three distinct entries in an expense report that sum to 2020 and multiply them together.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day01/shared/ with k = 3 sorted anchor + converging two-pointer scan (0.52 ms across 200 entries -> 140,379,120): reuses findKSumTuple, bounded two-pass traceKSumSearch, and ExpenseRepairVisualizer with gold A1 anchor + L/R markers, differentially verified across 30 seeded PRNG fixtures against an independent O(N^3) all-valid-products brute-force oracle.
learnings: Having a differential brute-force oracle return the full Set of all valid triple products avoids spurious mismatches on random fixtures that happen to contain multiple valid 2020 triples.
Pre-building generalized k-sum probing and A1/L/R visualizer tags in day01/shared/ let Part 2 land with zero shared edits.

parts.title: Password Philosophy
parts.summary: Count how many passwords in the corporate database contain their policy letter within the inclusive [min, max] occurrence range.
parts.algorithmSummary: Polymorphic PasswordValidationPolicy (SLED_RENTAL_POLICY for Part 1, pre-built TOBOGGAN_POLICY for zero-churn Part 2) in 2020/day02/shared/ (1.63 ms across 1,000 entries -> 447): immutable PasswordEntry/PasswordDatabase, zero-derived-state SledEvaluation/TobogganEvaluation, single-pass bounded tracePasswordAudit, interactive character-strip visualizer, differentially verified against an independent split-count oracle across 40 seeded fixtures.
parts.complexity: O(N * L) time, O(N * L) space
learnings: Polymorphic PolicyEvaluation classes (SledEvaluation & TobogganEvaluation) storing only entry and policy eliminate both stored derived state and type-tag switches in PasswordStrip.tsx.
Doing a full linear scan instead of early-exiting on count > max keeps displayed occurrence counts and matched character highlights truthful in the visualizer with negligible runtime cost.

parts.title: Password Philosophy
parts.summary: Count how many passwords contain their policy letter at exactly one of the two 1-based positions.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day02/shared/ binding TOBOGGAN_POLICY into countValidPasswords, tracePasswordAudit, and PasswordAuditVisualizer (1.19 ms across 1,000 entries -> 249): O(1) 1-based positional XOR evaluation handling equal positions and out-of-bounds slots branch-free, differentially verified against an independent 1-based XOR oracle across 40 seeded fixtures.
parts.complexity: O(N * L) parse & storage, O(N) solve
learnings: Pre-building TOBOGGAN_POLICY with independent slot probes (matchedIndices.length === 1) handled first === second and out-of-bounds slots cleanly with zero Part 2 shared edits.
Explicitly testing extra unchecked occurrences and 0-based off-by-one traps guards against Part 1 count logic leaking into Part 2.

parts.title: Toboggan Trajectory
parts.summary: Count the trees encountered while descending a horizontally tiling forest grid along slope right 3, down 1 from the top-left corner.
parts.algorithmSummary: Modular-stride slope evaluator over shared/core Grid2D and euclideanMod in 2020/day03/shared/ with PART2_SLOPES pre-built for zero-churn Part 2 (1.22 ms across 323x31 forest -> 237): zero-derived-state LandingStep/TrajectoryRun/SlopeProgress models, synchronized row-by-row bounded traceTrajectories, HiDPI 3-panel canvas visualizer (wrapped tile, unwrapped corridor, minimap) resolving CSS tokens via getComputedStyle, differentially verified against an explicit string-tiling oracle.
parts.complexity: O(H * W) parse, O(H / down) solve, O(1) auxiliary solve space
learnings: Canvas 2D fillStyle/strokeStyle cannot parse var(--token) strings directly, so resolving light-mode CSS tokens once via getComputedStyle(canvas) keeps HiDPI canvas rendering theme-consistent.
Modeling LandingStep with primary fields only (stepIndex, slope, forestCols, isTree) and deriving row, col, wrappedCol, and tileRepeat via getters eliminates state drift.

parts.title: Toboggan Trajectory
parts.summary: Multiply the tree counts encountered across all five slopes (1,1), (3,1), (5,1), (7,1), and (1,2) on the horizontally repeating forest grid.
parts.algorithmSummary: Zero-churn reuse of 2020/day03/shared/ binding PART2_SLOPES into createTobogganSolver and TobogganTrajectoryVisualizer (1.07 ms across 323x31 forest -> 2,106,818,610): exact BigInt 5-slope product, 5-slope focusable scoreboard & minimap canvas, differentially verified across 35 seeded PRNG grids (coprime/divisible widths and even/odd heights) against an explicit string-tiling oracle.
parts.complexity: O(R * C) parse, O(S * R) traversal time
learnings: Pre-building PART2_SLOPES and multi-slope synchronized tracing in day03/shared/ reduced Part 2's domain solver to 3 lines with zero shared-module edits.
Explicitly testing R = 2 ('#\n#' -> 0n) and crafted R = 3 zero-factor grids ensures down = 2 overshoot and zero-tree factors multiply cleanly in BigInt.
